en.headline: Less than 0.5 percent of nurses trained outside Hong Kong, authorities say
en.dek: Health officials released figures showing 99.8 percent of Hospital Authority nurses are locally trained, responding to union concerns over recruitment priorities.
body: Less than 0.5 percent of registered nurses in Hong Kong received their training outside the city, while about 99.8 percent of those working in public hospitals are locally trained, health authorities said on Tuesday.

The figures were released amid a dispute with a nursing union after claims that some Hospital Authority recruitment places were reserved for mainland Chinese nurses. A government spokesman said the number of non-locally trained registered nurses admitted through limited and special registration pathways remained very small as of the end of 2025.

Authorities emphasised that locally trained nurses remain the backbone of the public healthcare system and that the Hospital Authority continues to prioritise local graduates while addressing ongoing manpower shortages.

zh.headline: 當局指非本地培訓護士不足0.5% 公院本地培訓佔99.8%
zh.dek: 醫衞局及醫管局公布數據，回應工會關注招聘優先次序，強調本地培訓護士仍是公營醫療主力。
body: 當局周二表示，全港註冊護士中，非本地培訓者佔比不足0.5%，而醫管局轄下公營醫院的護士中，約99.8%為本地培訓。
數字是在護士工會提出五項訴求，包括優先聘用本地畢業生後公布。政府發言人指，透過有限度註冊及特別註冊途徑引入的非本地培訓註冊護士數目，截至2025年底仍然很少。
當局重申本地培訓護士是公營醫療系統的骨幹，醫管局會繼續優先考慮本地畢業生，同時應對人手短缺問題。
